description: Installable Candidate reproducing MiaAI-Lab's public 6f7d1590 kit (release 2026-09-19, no upstream version tag) by running her published image ghcr.io/miaai-lab/deepseek-v4.1-flash-exl3-2x-dgx-sparks (tag 2.9bpw, sha256:2f0cf3adc0f989c1d446be274df864eb799630175f604c3b22b71b7205971dce, the digest the kit's docs pin) as published, not rebuilding it from the kit's Dockerfile (a thin layer adds the Controller launcher, the Responses text-content patch the kit applies at container start, and the non-root user), serving: the 196 GiB Mia-AiLab EXL3 2.9 bpw checkpoint at 64ba41b6, tensor-parallel 2 over the Spark fabric, native DSpark (k=3), file-backed Engram tables read from shards 47 and 48 of the official deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash checkpoint (dba1be0a, declared as a second Model, about 189 GiB per node), 600k context, 2 sequences, a 2.5 GiB pinned KV pool, vision input and tools. Chosen over sfxnz's 3de91468 kit (MIT, 2.0 bpw pack, claims 39.6 tok/s greedy) because it is a published prebuilt image, the higher-quality 2.9 bpw pack and the closest sibling of the existing Mia EXL3 recipe; sfxnz's kit needs a chain of patch images, a 334 GB pack and further first-use kernel compilation. The kit source is AGPL-3.0 with earlier MIT contributions (upstream-LICENSE, upstream-LICENSE-MIT); both Models are MIT. Upstream claims (not measured here): about 23 to 39 tok/s single stream depending on workload, 774,400-token KV pool, and a first boot of about 25 minutes. Not exposed: the cooperative-MoE binary (needs an unpinned prebuilt library), Engram row packing (a host-side artifact), the language-model-only switch, the memory-guard watchdog and the third-party abliterated overlay. The engine-ready timeout is 3600 s (upstream 1500 s) because upstream reports a first boot of about 25 minutes. Thinking is on by default (reasoning effort high), so a small max_tokens can return empty content unless chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking is false. Vonk physical acceptance is pending. Memory follows the creator's settings: gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 beside the fixed 2,684,354,560-byte (2.5 GiB) KV pool, as in MiaAI-Lab's .env.example at 6f7d1590 (lines 146 and 151); with a pinned pool the utilization is only vLLM's startup free-memory check (line 143). The declared peak, 115,984,824,099 bytes, is the loading floor: the weights per rank, the pool and 8 GB of runtime overhead; the reserve is 8 GB, and admission keeps the platform memory floor free beside the peak.
title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash EXL3 2.9 bpw Mia two Sparks
